author: BBC News
description:
China has warned that President Trump''s decision to mount a naval blockade of Iran's ports is "dangerous and irresponsible" and threatens the recent ceasefire in the Middle East.

The US navy has begun blockading the strait of Hormuz, following the failure of peace talks between American and Iranian negotiators in Pakistan. 

US Central Command says it has prevented any ships from passing through the strait since it began the blockade.

Russian and Chinese foreign ministers have been meeting to discuss the Iran crisis.   The Chinese said the blockade would escalate tension and undermine the fragile ceasefire.   China is a major buyer of Iranian oil and an ally of Tehran. 

Donald Trump has unexpectedly announced that new peace talks with Iran may begin within the next two days. 

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Frank Gardner and Sarah Smith.

Lebanon and Israel have held their first diplomatic talks in over three decades - a rare encounter aimed at ending fighting between Israel and the Iran-backed Hezbollah group.
 
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who mediated the meeting in Washington, said it was a "historic opportunity" to end Hezbollah's influence.
 
Meanwhile, the US said no ships passed through its blockade on the Strait of Hormuz in the first 24 hours, and six merchant vessels turned around after "direction from US forces".
 
China has called the blockade "irresponsible and dangerous".

The image, which has now been deleted, showed Trump appearing to heal a sick man in a hospital bed. He said it showed him as a doctor. The image post came hours after the president posted a lengthy message criticising the pontiff, who is a vocal critic of the US and Israeli military operation in Iran.

description:
At least four Iran-linked ships - including two that visited Iranian ports - crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday following the start of a blockade by the US. At least three others also crossed the key shipping channel.
 
China's foreign ministry condemned the blockade of Iranian ports as "dangerous and irresponsible" - a spokesman has warmed it would only "exacerbate tensions”.
 
Washington's blockade came into force on Monday. US Vice-President JD Vance accused the Iranian government of engaging in an "act of economic terrorism" by blocking traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
 
Vance added that US President Donald Trump has shown that "two could play at that game".

author: BBC News
description:
What does the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz mean and why is the US imposing it on Iranian ports? 

At least four Iran-linked ships, including two that visited Iranian ports, crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday following the start of a blockade by the US.

The US military says it "will not impede" ships using the strait to go to and from non-Iranian ports. Iran says the blockade is a violation of its sovereignty. 

The blockade and escalating threats come after weeks of Iran being in control of one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes.   

And over the weekend, delegates from the US and Iran failed to reach a resolution after 21 hours of peace talks.  

The Trump administration has repeatedly insisted it’s winning the war, but so has the government in Tehran, which believes it is negotiating from a position of power.   

To help us understand why - and what Iran wants - Tristan and Asma are joined by Parham Ghobadi from the BBC Persian Service.

description:
Police in Greece have been recruiting migrants to violently push other migrants back across its land border with Turkey, according to wide-ranging evidence uncovered by the BBC.
 
Pushbacks - forcing migrants and asylum seekers back across borders without due process - are generally considered illegal under international law.
 
The Greek prime minister told the BBC he was "totally unaware" about allegations of the use of migrants for pushbacks, while the country's authorities have not responded to our written detailed requests for comment.
